Author: Hansen Michael Motet
Message:
Start a sprint and close a story from the desk: validate, close --check, label-or-number sprints, /sprint and /close (#25)

dis-agent validate runs the independent tester on demand (--branch main for an already merged story; new tests go on a PR branch).
close --check previews the evidence without prompting. -s accepts the sprint label or the number the board shows, with an
error that lists the sprints that have plans; po and planning default to the next free number. /sprint walks a sprint start
step by step and /close shows the evidence then closes only if every gate passes; neither passes --force.

Co-authored-by: Michael.Hansen <motethansen@gmail.com>

Author: Hansen Michael Motet
Message:
Scrum flow: PO/SM/dispatch CLI, integrator role, DeepSeek on listed projects, isolation, Opus cap fallback (#13)

po and plan write proposal files for a human; dispatch queues role/project/sprint/story-tagged tasks
in dependency waves only with --go, adds an integrator after DeepSeek code and a reviewer after every dev
task, and stops at the first failure. DeepSeek never gets sensitive work or a prompt that looks like it
carries a credential; urbanlife needs explicit approval; a spent Opus cap falls back instead of refusing.

Co-authored-by: Michael.Hansen <motethansen@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Author: Michael.Hansen
Message:
feat(clients): fleet-mcp — use the distributed agents from any MCP harness

A stdio MCP server that gives Claude Code (and T3 Code's Claude threads), Codex,
OpenCode, Antigravity and pi the tools fleet_ask, fleet_result, fleet_tasks,
fleet_machines and fleet_end_conversation. It submits agent_run tasks to the
orchestrator (tries both active orchestrators), so the agents run on the workers
under their own subscription/API logins with the usage-limit failover. Named
conversations keep recent turns locally (data/, gitignored), so a chat started in
one harness can continue in another — e.g. Codex after Claude hits its limit.

SECRET_KEY is read from the repo .env, never from a harness config. Reports to
Vantage as component fleet-mcp. 10 tests against a fake orchestrator;
mutation-checked (history, reply recording, orchestrator fallback).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Author: Michael.Hansen
Message:
Report each machine's current LAN addresses and Tailscale path in /machines

LAN addresses drift (DHCP, randomised Wi-Fi MACs: mac-mini went .21 -> .105 -> .46 ->
.101 -> .204), so Tailscale is the primary address but you still need the LAN one to
get at a machine when the overlay is down. Workers now heartbeat to every orchestrator
each cycle with {iface: ip} (Tailscale, docker, loopback, link-local and inactive
interfaces excluded); /machines shows lan_ips, tailscale_path (direct | relay:<region>)
and tailscale_addr. A relay path between two machines in the same house is itself an alarm.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
